source.title: Orbiters overhead
source.mission: Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter, 2001 Mars Odyssey, Mars Express, ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter
source.instrument: Trajectory predictions from each mission's navigation team, served by JPL Horizons
source.agency: NASA JPL (Horizons); ESA for Mars Express and TGO trajectories
source.productId: JPL Horizons observer tables: sub-observer point (quantity 14) and azimuth and elevation (quantity 4)
source.gridSpacing: One point every 2 minutes on the globe; every 1 minute at a site
source.realDetail: Whole degrees of elevation; ground points to 0.01 degree
source.positionAccuracy: not found: Horizons does not state the error of a prediction, which grows along the orbit with time
source.processing: Horizons gives Mars longitude west-positive and latitude on its reference ellipsoid; converted to east longitude and planetocentric latitude. Each site's position is sent to Horizons as planetodetic latitude and west longitude, and the longitude Horizons echoes is checked.
caveats: Predicted positions, not tracked ones. Each orbiter's notes say how far its trajectory is fitted to tracking.
TGO's trajectory is fitted to tracking only up to June 2025, so its times are the least certain.
Above the horizon does not mean a link is scheduled, or that a camera is pointed at you.
MAVEN is left out: Horizons notes no contact since 6 December 2025.
source.credit: NASA JPL Horizons, with trajectories from NASA and ESA mission navigation teams
